transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (CSM), Maya (HelioRx Head of ML), Omar (Platform Eng), Lena (Security), Daniel (Product)

Summary (auto): Quarterly health + advisory. Focus on cost spike in Jan, infra mitigation, and private deployment questions. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving the time out, um so this is the Q1 advisory sync for HelioRx. quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: Maya here.
[00:09] Omar: Omar on the platform side.
[00:11] Lena: Lena, security.
[00:12] Daniel: Daniel product.
[00:14] Jordan: Great. Priya and Samir from Redwood are here as well. We'll go through usage, reliability, then security questions and roadmap.
[00:25] Priya: I'll kick off with a quick surface level of what we saw in January — there was a notable usage spike starting Jan 12, looks like a combination of higher prompt length and a batch of synthetic QA jobs that ran longer than usual. that increased token counts and triggered some burst billing.
[00:40] Maya: yeah that was on our side — we had a campaign that regenerates long transcripts for compliance, forgot to throttle the beam size.
[00:47] Omar: question — when you say burst billing, is that from hosted API or our dedicated pool?
[00:52] Jordan: it's primarily hosted for the extra jobs; your dedicated pool handled steady-state, but the short-lived jobs overflowed to hosted which is why costs spiked.
[00:59] Maya: ah ok, that explains it. we thought maybe the KV cache wasn't warming.
[01:03] Priya: there were cache misses early in the job run, especially for longer prefix sequences. also noticed some long tail latency at about 95th/99th; that's where the user experience hit.
[01:15] Lena: can you unpack the tail latency bit? is this pre-empted by queuing, or is it model-side?
[01:21] Priya: good q — looks like a combo: burst routing to hosted endpoints, extra cold starts for larger sequence lengths, and some batching inefficiencies for these odd-shaped requests. the runtime is optimized for continuous batching so unusual seq distribution spikes efficiency loss.
[01:35] Daniel: so what's the mitigation — do we go to more dedicated capacity or tune batching? what's fastest?
[01:41] Jordan: short term: tune batching + set a prefix cache for those long transcripts. Priya can push a KV cache warmup suggestion. medium term: reserved capacity with auto-burst config so those jobs don't overflow.
[01:52] Priya: yes, and we have a config we can apply per route: reduce max batch wait, increase max batch tokens for that route, and prewarm KV entries. we'll include the precise CLI / config snippet.
[02:05] Maya: good. about cost — can you show committed vs on-demand numbers?
[02:09] Jordan: we will. Samir, did we capture the cost delta in the latest spreadsheet?
[02:13] Samir: I have a quick split: January extra hosted overflow was ~24% above forecast for that workload. If HelioRx were on a small committed plan (reserved), you would have covered ~70% of those extra tokens at lower unit cost. I'll send a comparison break down.
[02:26] Omar: also want to understand CPU/GPU utilization on dedicated nodes — is there a way to see per-model utilization?
[02:31] Priya: yes, console exposes per-model and per-route token throughput, broken down by GPU utilization and queue depth. we can map the HelioRx model variants to those metrics and share a dashboard link.
[02:41] Lena: Security: KMS question — do you support customer-managed keys, and how are keys rotated? also audit log retention?
[02:48] Jordan: we support bring-your-own KMS for Private deployments (HSM integration optional). for hosted, we provide KMS with customer-managed keys through partner KMS options, and rotation policies are documented. Samir will send a security packet.
[02:58] Lena: and audit logs, we need 7 years retention for certain customers — any limits on retention?
[03:04] Samir: hosted default retention is 1 year; on Private we can configure longer retention and ship logs to customer S3 or Kinesis for archival. will need HelioRx to enumerate required fields.
[03:14] Lena: i'll send that.
[03:16] Maya: a couple of other asks — can you run a stress test that mimics our production pattern (lots of mid-sized prompts, occasional long transcripts) and show P95/P99 and cost impact?
[03:26] Priya: absolutely, we can run that. we'll need a small sample prompt set and token distribution; can you drop that in the shared drive?
[03:32] Omar: i'll drop a sanitized sample today.
[03:35] Priya: great. we'll run benchmarks including KV-cache warmup scenarios and show numbers for hosted vs dedicated with our recommended batching tweaks.
[03:45] Daniel: timeline-wise, we need a pilot-to-dedicated plan by mid-Feb if budget allows — what's realistic?
[03:51] Jordan: realistic: 2-4 weeks to configure dedicated pool and do basic validations; deeper network/VPC entitlements add time. If the infra folks are ready we can accelerate.
[03:59] Omar: what's involved with VPC peering / Private deployment? we have strict firewall rules and need to keep some traffic on-prem.
[04:05] Priya: for Redwood Private, we provide a control plane and options: managed VPC connectors, or an on-prem appliance. connectivity can be VPN or direct connect, and data plane can be inside your VPC. we have a checklist for ports, CIDRs, and auth that we'll share.
[04:19] Lena: about SSO / RBAC — we need SAML + SCIM provisioning and role separation, plus auditability for admin actions.
[04:26] Jordan: supported. enterprise SSO with SAML/SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, and audit trail for admin ops. Samir will capture exact endpoints and the SCIM attributes.
[04:36] Maya: any concerns about model quality regressions if we quantize or change variants to save cost?
[04:42] Priya: there can be quality delta; Redwood Optimize recommends model/quant profiles per workload. we suggest A/B rollout for quantized variants and tie quality alerts to a small canonical eval set that you own.
[04:53] Daniel: can you host the eval and run regression monitors?
[04:56] Priya: yes we offer evaluation hooks and delta alerts; we'll propose thresholding settings in the follow-up doc.
[05:04] Jordan: quick pause — want to confirm deliverables: pricing sheet, benchmark run, security packet, rollback playbook, and VPC checklist. Samir will own security packet, Priya benchmark, Jordan pricing + commit options.
[05:18] Samir: noted. Lena, Maya — can you confirm decision timeline?
[05:22] Maya: we aim to decide on committed capacity by next Friday 2/13, maybe earlier if numbers look good.
[05:28] Lena: security review needs to be complete before production flip, so prefer 2/20 for final sign-off.
[05:33] Jordan: excellent, we'll target those dates.
[05:36] Daniel: one small nit — in the console, when an overflow happens, we saw confusing route names; can we have clearer labeling for our routes?
[05:41] Priya: yes that'll be an easy config change, we'll help rename routes and add aliasing so the dashboard maps to your internal service names.
[05:48] Omar: any blockers for us to move a few hours of traffic to dedicated as a test?
[05:52] Jordan: just logistics: we need a signed mini-commit and network connectivity; we can standby on the rest.
[05:57] Maya: ok i'll coordinate with finance and infra and update by end of next week.
[06:02] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:06] (crosstalk) Samir: i'll put the security packet in the shared folder now.

End of transcript.
